name: World War II Service Award (full-size medal body)
size_basis: Body width 1.375 in = the standard ribbon width for this size (1 3/8 in full, 5/8 in miniature; DoDM 1348.33 as relayed by the coordination chat, not verified locally); proportions from the McChord rasters (disc = ribbon width); CAPR 39-3 gives no medal dimensions. Height is the constructed body plus suspension ring.

ribbon_ref.note: medal body only; the ribbon asset supplies the stripes and devices. ribbon_attach is where the ribbon meets the suspension loop.

source: Designed and measured from the Vanguard photograph wartime-wwii-service.jpeg (reference only): disc, rim, lettering, emblem, bail and ring are parametric shapes in inches, the same model as the miniature drawn at 2.2x (design/wwii.js). Previously constructed from the McChord rasters.

fit.metric: same model as the miniature body, which is gated against the photograph (silhouette IoU, landmarks within 0.02 in, edge recall)
fit.note: Shape-built art at 2.2x, upright; ring and bail are cut open at the box top where the box cuts them.

measured.photo: wartime-wwii-service.jpeg (Vanguard photograph, 600 x 600 px, reference only)

frame.note: body width 0.625 in (the spec width) sets the scale; every length below is inches in the medal frame (origin = disc centre, +y down, UPRIGHT: the photograph is rotated by the measured hang angle into this frame)

measured.hang_angle_note: measured from the bail axis against the disc centre in the photograph (frame.js); the drawing hangs upright (bail and disc axis vertical)
not_measurable: The photograph's engraving grain, wear and specular highlights are not drawn (flat tones).

The suspension ring is hidden by the ribbon above its lower third: its centre and radius are fitted to the visible lower arcs (0.134 in outer radius), the upper part is assumed circular; the full body shows it complete.
The rim is a plain flat band: the photograph shows no separate ridge, so the rim annulus (0.2985 to 0.3095 in) is the lit band itself.

The engraved star outline and the rays are thin lines near the resolution of the photograph (one pixel = 0.0035 in): their widths (0.004 and 0.0075 in) are set from the blurred line profile; the star valleys on the diagonals lie under the hub circle and are placed (0.104 in) from the straight edges that run into them.
Letter stroke 0.0078 in is judged from the zoom comparison, thinner than the threshold-blurred 0.0095 in.
